The resolution sets how the House meets, forms committees, handles bills and amendments, and what kinds of bills and resolutions can be considered. It took effect when adopted.

NC-2025-SB857.aiSummary: The law updates rules for the Funeral Service Board and some licensing rules. It says a funeral establishment that uses a living person's name must have that person licensed as a funeral director or funeral service licensee, or have had a licensed person meet the board's rules when the first permit was issued. It also bars misleading funeral establishment names, including some plural names, deceased names, and names of people not tied to the business.

NC-2025-SB648.aiSummary: The bill would change a landlord-tenant law on eviction costs. It would let a landlord recover certain lawyer fees from a tenant in some cases, including when the landlord wins and when a court finds the tenant’s appeal was frivolous, unreasonable, without basis, in bad faith, or just meant to delay the case. The change would apply back to September 9, 2024.

NC-2025-SB1074.aiSummary: The law lets Eden make an agreement with Duke Energy that can block forced annexation of certain Dan River plant land from July 1, 2025, through June 30, 2030, in return for $1,000,000 paid in five yearly $200,000 payments. It also cancels any unified development ordinance the Town of Mills River adopted between June 30, 2025, and July 1, 2026. For Guilford County, it changes the rules for a local 0.25% sales tax referendum and how the tax money would be split and used if voters approve it.

NC-2025-HB1222.aiSummary: The act would give the Brunswick County Board of Commissioners the final say on certain land use decisions, including some subdivision plats, special use permits, zoning changes, and variances. It would also require traffic impact studies for certain development projects and have those studies presented in open meetings before a vote. The board’s final votes on these matters would have to be recorded so the public record shows how each member voted, and the rule would apply only in Brunswick County outside city zoning areas.

NC-2025-HB34.aiSummary: This bill would tighten rules for Medicaid providers in North Carolina. It would change the grounds for adverse termination, including false claims for services not provided, falsifying medical records, and not repaying a final overpayment of more than $1,500. It would also allow action for conduct that may put Medicaid patients or the program at risk, and it would add the words "lawfully present" in one place.
